title: Heat Pump Water Heater Rebates in Penticton 2026: Up to $1,000
desc: Penticton's electric customers can claim up to $1,000 from FortisBC for a heat pump water heater replacing a standard electric tank. 63% own. Rules and installers.
h1: Heat Pump Water Heater Rebates in Penticton
lead: Penticton buys power from the City's electric utility, and FortisBC's listing covers its customers. FortisBC pays $1,000 for replacing a standard electric tank with a heat pump model.
cards_heading: What heat pump water heater rebates pay in Penticton
cards_intro: We read FortisBC's heat pump water heater listing on October 2, 2026. It pays $1,000 when you replace a standard electric storage tank. If you are switching from another fuel, FortisBC points to CleanBC instead.

cards.title: FortisBC
cards.note: For replacing a standard electric storage tank with a high-efficiency heat pump water heater.

cards.title: Second-upgrade bonus
cards.note: FortisBC adds $300 for a second upgrade, or an EnerGuide improvement bonus of $750 to $2,000.

cards.title: Income-qualified (CleanBC)
cards.note: Level 1 households replacing a fossil-fuel or electric water heater. Level 2 gets up to $2,800 from electric. Primary water heater only.

cards.title: Lower incomes (FortisBC)
cards.note: Income-qualified customers can get free evaluations and upgrades.

sections: Who in Penticton can use this

The 2021 Census counted 17,360 households in Penticton. About 63% own, 40% live in detached houses and 36% in apartments. Of the households, 3,440 own a detached house built before 1981. Penticton's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was -2.5°C.

The rebate is only for replacing an electric water heater. If your tank runs on natural gas, BC Hydro and FortisBC do not pay for a switch to a heat pump model. Lower-income households can use the CleanBC Energy Savings Program, which pays up to $3,500 for Level 1 households converting from a fossil fuel. Only one primary water heating rebate is allowed per home across programs.

A heat pump water heater pulls warmth from the air around it, so where it sits matters. Ask the installer how much open space the model needs, how loud it runs, where the condensate drains, and what happens in a cold utility room. These are not program rules, but they decide whether you like the tank after the first winter. Get the answers in the quote.

BC Hydro's page offers a bonus of up to $2,000 when you complete more than one eligible upgrade, such as insulation or windows with your water heater. The formula is not on the page, so ask when you apply. FortisBC lists a $300 second-upgrade bonus. A water heater is a quick job, so it is an easy second item to add to a larger project.

BC Hydro's rebate needs a BC Hydro account. FortisBC's listing is open to its gas customers and to FortisBC or municipal electric customers, including Penticton. If you are switching from another energy source, FortisBC points you to CleanBC.

claim_steps: Check that the tank you are replacing is electric and is your primary water heater.
Pick a model from NEEA's Tier 2 or higher list and get it on the quote.
Have a licensed contractor install it and keep the invoice.
Apply online within six months of the invoice date.
If your income is lower, ask about the CleanBC program before paying.
